div.head: I Em 6
div.ab: Ða ðe mansweriað ⁊ lyblat wyrcað syn hy á fram ælcum Godes dæle aworpene, buten hy to rihtre dædbote gecyrran.
Ða ðe mansweriað ⁊ liblac wyrcað, beon hi a fram ælcum Godes dæle aworpene, buton hi to rihtre dædbote gecirran þe geornor.
Ða ðe mánsweriað ⁊ lyblat wyrcað, syn hy a fram ælcum Godes dæle aworpene, bute hy to rihtre dædbote gecyrran.
Qui falsum iurabunt uel liblatum facient, sint in eternum á Dei consortio segregati, nisi ad dignam satisfactionem per omnia reuertantur.
[Be mánsworum ⁊ liblacum.] [Ld] Ða ðe mansweriað ⁊ liblac wyrcað beon hi a fram ælcum Godes dæle aworpene, buton hi to rihtre dædbote gecirran þe geornor.
Ða ðe mansweriað and liblac wyrcað beon hi a fram ælcum Godes dæle aworpene buton hi to rihtre dædbote gecirran þe geornor.

(Über Meineidige und Zaubereien. Ld) Die, welche falsch schwören und Zauberei üben, sie seien immerfort von jedem Antheil an Gott[es Kirche] verstossen, es sei denn, sie bekehren sich zu gesetzlicher Kirchenbusse (um so eifriger D).

(Of perjurers and sorcery. Ld) Those who swear falsely and practise sorcery, let them be cast out for ever from any share in God['s church], unless they turn to lawful penance (all the more eagerly, D).
Those who commit perjury, and practise sorcery shall be cast out for ever from the fellowship of God, unless they proceed with special zeal to undertake the prescribed penance.
Those who commit perjury and work magic are to be expelled forever from the communion of God unless they embark upon the proper penance all the more zealously.

note.label: echoes
note.quote: Æthelstan forbade Christian burial for the perjured. He was echoed in his brother’s first code

div.note: In D, the rubric ‘Her gebirað nu to Eadgares gerædnes be gehadodra manna liffadunge’ (i.e. the Canons of Edgar) follows; in H and B, II Em follows on a new line. Liebermann compares II As 26.
embark . . . all the more zealously: Omitted from Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 383, Textus Roffensis, and Quadripartitus. Likely an interpolation by Wulfstan.
